spans.text: # CP-0 — TDG annual source readiness
Run: `tdg-001`, 2026-11-04. This is a new model-authored response in the current
assistant session, using local file tools. It is not a historical reconstruction,
an isolated provider run or proof of the imported runtime.
Instructions: [CP-0](../../prompts/CP-0.md), SHA-256
Method selection: Deploy V `c4d2e356` ancestry; Deploy Workflow method tree
`6f4a3997e7356352898c410cb7a045722aa5bf03` at selected revision
`2c809379cbba508888b7fbe28ee14eac5a294bbf`; targeted coverage and consumer-readiness
amendments recorded in [the methodology review](../../METHODOLOGY-REVIEW.md).
The linked prompt defines this bounded check, not certification of every CP-0 duty.
## Request
Determine whether the supplied TDG annual PDF can support CP-1 extraction of its
annual primary financial statements and comparative columns. Quarterly analysis,
current covenant compliance, adjusted metrics and a complete credit report are
outside this request.
## Sources
- **S1:** [TDG annual report PDF](../../data/public-corpus/v1/TDG/TDG_FY2024_annual-report_SEC-PDF_0001260221-25-000008_a841225transdigmgroupbookm.pdf).
- Project-root-relative source path:
`data/public-corpus/v1/TDG/TDG_FY2024_annual-report_SEC-PDF_0001260221-25-000008_a841225transdigmgroupbookm.pdf`.
- SHA-256: `dc6a8ea6249e4e919d190a4bbb459d9bf4eded005b7d5680ae911b32d44d44af`.
- Size: 4,378,190 bytes; 160 PDF pages. Page numbers below are **one-based PDF
pages**, not the printed page labels.
- Fresh text extraction: [source-pages.jsonl](source-pages.jsonl), one record per
PDF page, using the project's installed pypdf in layout mode. This is a reading
aid; S1 remains the evidence. No historical model output was used as a source.
- Authority: the document identifies itself as a Form 10-K and includes an audit
opinion. This check establishes its contents, not a fresh SEC download or
authentication. No conflicting version was supplied to this check; versions
outside S1 were not compared. No draft marker was observed on the examined pages.
## Findings
### Identity, periods and presentation
| Finding | Located evidence in S1 |
| Registrant is TransDigm Group Incorporated; document is its FY2024 Form 10-K. | PDF 1: “TransDigm Group Incorporated”; “FORM 10-K”; “For the fiscal year ended September 30, 2024”. |

| Consolidated TD Group and subsidiaries, rather than a standalone subsidiary or guarantor perimeter. | PDF 110: “include the accounts of TD Group and subsidiaries. Intercompany balances and transactions have been eliminated.” |
| U.S. GAAP presentation. | PDF 110: “The accompanying consolidated financial statements were prepared in conformity with U.S. GAAP”. |
| Reporting currency is USD. | PDF 55: “Because our consolidated financial statements are presented in U.S. dollars”. |
| Fiscal-year convention ends September 30; FY2024 is October 1, 2023 through September 30, 2024. | PDF 3: “the year ending or ended September 30.”; “October 1, 2023 to September 30, 2024.” |
| Balance sheets are instants at September 30, 2024 and 2023. They do not have duration start dates. | PDF 105: “AS OF SEPTEMBER 30, 2024 AND 2023”. |

| Income, comprehensive income, changes in stockholders' deficit and cash flows cover FY2024, FY2023 and FY2022. The equity statement also opens at September 30, 2021. | PDF 101 statement index; PDF 106–109 headings and dated rows. The fiscal-year convention on PDF 3 supplies the annual duration starts; the equity opening balance is not a fourth income-statement period. |

| The audit opinion covers the two balance-sheet dates and three fiscal years. | PDF 103: “in conformity with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles.” The opinion is read as evidence of the document's accounting basis, not a new assurance opinion by this module. |

| Comparative reclassifications are disclosed. | PDF 110: “prior year amounts to conform to the current year presentation, none of which are material.” Use the comparative columns in this filing and retain this qualification. |
### Page map for CP-1
| Content | PDF page(s) | Printed label | Unit / period instruction |
| Fiscal-year convention | 3 | 1 | September 30 year-end; explicit FY2024 start/end. |
| Reporting currency | 55 | 53 | USD, supported by the explicit currency statement above. |
| Financial statement index | 101 | 99 | Resolves statement and note locations. |
| Audit opinion | 103–104 | F-1–F-2 | Opinion text examined on 103; 104 located as continuation. |
| Consolidated balance sheets | 105 | F-3 | “Amounts in millions, except share amounts”; instants 2024-09-30 and 2023-09-30. Preserve embedded per-share par value separately. |

| Consolidated statements of income | 106 | F-4 | “Amounts in millions, except per share amounts”; annual 2024/2023/2022. Monetary rows are USD millions; EPS and dividends per share are USD/share; weighted-average shares are millions of shares. |
| Consolidated statements of comprehensive income | 107 | F-5 | “Amounts in millions”; annual 2024/2023/2022. |

| Consolidated statements of changes in stockholders' deficit | 108 | F-6 | “Amounts in millions, except share amounts”; annual changes and dated opening/closing balances. Actual share counts and embedded dividends per share require their own quantity families. |

| Consolidated statements of cash flows | 109 | F-7 | “Amounts in millions”; annual 2024/2023/2022. Parentheses carry sign; retain source dashes without silently treating every dash as missing or zero. |
| Basis and consolidation policy | 110 | F-8 | Consolidation, U.S. GAAP and comparative reclassification qualification. |
| Notes, for targeted follow-up | 110–153 | F-8–F-51 | Located from the index. Full note coverage has not been reviewed. |
Additional routing, **not completed analysis**: non-GAAP definition/bridges on
PDF 52–54; debt on 126–133; taxes on 137; segment information/reconciliation on
141–142; leases on 147–148. Read the actual passages if a later request needs
these topics. The rotated supplemental reconciliation on 156 is subject to G1.
### Coverage actually examined

## Request

Extract and interpret the annual financial foundation from the sole supplied issuer filing, with complete primary statements, relevant supplemental schedules, explicit gaps and consumer readiness. Scope is TransDigm Group Incorporated and consolidated subsidiaries, FY2022–FY2024, plus the September 30, 2023 and 2024 balance sheet instants. No quarterly, YTD or LTM series is constructed.
## Sources

**S1 — issuer source:** TransDigm Group Incorporated Form 10-K for fiscal year ended September 30, 2024. PDF: `data/public-corpus/v1/TDG/TDG_FY2024_annual-report_SEC-PDF_0001260221-25-000008_a841225transdigmgroupbookm.pdf`; SHA-256 `dc6a8ea6249e4e919d190a4bbb459d9bf4eded005b7d5680ae911b32d44d44af` (matches CP-0). Fresh text aid is `runs/tdg-001/source-pages.jsonl`; PDF pages below are one-based PDF page numbers, not printed labels. Text aid used for statement extraction and note reading; primary statement cells were cross-checked against the page text and PDF images retained by CP-0 for pages 105, 106 and 109. Relevant supplemental PDF pages 45–46 (facility terms, outstanding letters of credit and note maturities), 52–54 (non-GAAP definitions and both EBITDA bridges), 126–133 (debt), 141–142 (segments and EBITDA As Defined), 147–148 (leases), and 137 (tax) were read from the aid; no visual cell audit is claimed for these schedules.

Issuer is TransDigm Group Incorporated. The filing defines “Company” as TD Group with TransDigm Inc. and wholly/majority-owned subsidiaries under control (PDF 3); consolidation policy says statements include TD Group and subsidiaries with intercompany balances/transactions eliminated and uses U.S. GAAP (PDF 110). Currency is USD (PDF 55). FY convention is October 1 through September 30 (PDF 3). Annual income, comprehensive income, equity changes and cash-flow periods cover FY2022, FY2023 and FY2024; balance-sheet dates are September 30, 2023 and September 30, 2024 (PDF 105–109). Monetary statement amounts are USD millions unless noted. EPS/dividend per share are USD per share; weighted-average shares are millions of shares; share counts are individual shares. Balance-sheet amounts are instants, not duration flows.

The audit report states the consolidated financial statements were audited and opines fair presentation in conformity with U.S. GAAP (PDF 103). CP-0 notes that external authenticity/latest-version status was not independently checked and comparative reclassifications to conform to current presentation were disclosed as not material (PDF 110). Source authority is therefore the supplied filed annual report; this module does not authenticate an SEC download.

Subsequent event reviewed: the company drew the remaining $162.5 million available under the trade receivable securitization facility in October 2024 (PDF 131). This is post-period financing and is not added to September 30 reported debt or historical cash. CP-0 G1 about rotated PDF 156 remains unresolved because that supplemental non-GAAP table is outside this extraction; G2 cell/glyph verification remains a limitation for unvisually reviewed pages and notes; G3 external version/authenticity remains unexamined. PDF 156 is not needed for the extracted primary statements or EBITDA As Defined bridge on PDF 142.

The expense block is selling and administrative expenses plus amortization of intangible assets; calculated aggregate expense magnitude is 884, 919 and 1,141 in FY2022–FY2024, respectively, as bridged in Calculations and the transcript. Segment sales span Power & Control, Airframe and Non-aviation; the full channel/category figures and reconciliations are in T4.16, PDF 141. This evidence supports annual growth and mix description, but does not isolate price, volume, acquisition or organic causes.

Net cash provided by operating activities increased from 948 in FY2022 to 2,045 in FY2024, while the FY2024 cash-flow statement reports capital expenditures of (165), acquisition of businesses net of cash acquired of (2,347), and net cash used in investing activities of (2,441); see the correspondingly named rows in T4.5, PDF 109. EBITDA and EBITDA As Defined are issuer non-GAAP measures; PDF 52 warns against treating them as alternatives to GAAP net income or operating cash flow and cites their limitations. The annual evidence supports historical description, but not current covenant headroom, future refinancing capacity or a forward liquidity conclusion.

See the new exact Decimal transcript `runs/tdg-002/CP-1-attempt-2-calculations.txt`; it identifies statement table, source row, year and operands for every check. Principal reconciliations:

- Balance sheet: liabilities plus total deficit/equity equals assets at both balance dates.

- Issuer net-income and cash-flow bridges to EBITDA / EBITDA As Defined (FY2024 and FY2023) each reconcile at zero residual; the full three-year segment reconciliation on PDF 142 separately reconciles each year to pretax income.
- FY2024 OCF less capex yields 1,880; defined only as subtraction, not issuer FCF.
- Full line-level cash-flow sums, segment component sums, comprehensive-income totals, all equity movement columns, debt maturity schedules and debt carrying bridges are checked in the transcript.

T4.12 is the gap register below. T4.13 is the consumer readiness assessment in Next module. T4.19 reconciliation results are in Calculations and the dedicated attempt-2 transcript.

| G5 | The reviewed facility terms disclose 843 of available borrowings and 67 of letters of credit outstanding against 910 of commitments, but do not identify a funded revolver drawing in that passage or provide a current borrowing-base certificate. The filing’s EBITDA As Defined bridge is not a full independent covenant calculation; definitions and usage are bounded by its cited terms. | Review credit agreement/updated facility certificates if exact availability or covenant headroom is needed. |

| G6 | Cash-after-capex is calculable but no issuer maintenance/growth capex split or single universally defined FCF series is supplied by the statements. | Use OCF and capex source rows directly; do not label simple subtraction as issuer FCF. |

| G7 | Dividend declared, payable, and cash paid are different; no per-share cash payment allocation by period can be derived from total cash payments. | Keep separate and obtain detailed distribution records if cash dividend per share is required. |

| G8 | Complete note coverage was not performed; acquisition purchase-price effects and all add-back eligibility/cash status were not audited here. | Target specific notes and supporting schedules before transaction-adjusted earnings or earnings-quality classification. |
## Next module

**CP-1A business/transaction context:** can use entity, audited annual history, segments, acquisition cash spending and identified source limits. Transaction-specific pro forma revenue/earnings and quarterly bridge remain missing.

**CP-1B earnings delta:** can compare annual reported FY2022–FY2024 statements, including expense block and issuer EBITDA As Defined. Cannot establish quarter-to-quarter or transaction-adjusted delta; do not mix amortization/D&A definitions.

**CP-1D earnings quality:** can examine annual cash conversion, working-capital changes, cash taxes/interest, capex, acquisitions, and the issuer’s EBITDA bridge. Limited by no detailed cash/noncash testing of every add-back, no maintenance/growth capex split and no independent note-level verification.

**CP-2 fundamental credit:** can consume annual assets/liabilities, cash, debt carrying amounts, selected principal/facility/maturity terms, cash flows and reported EBITDA As Defined with its limitations. The filing reports covenant compliance for Secured and Subordinated Notes, but this module does not calculate or independently verify covenant compliance; current liquidity, complete debt waterfall and transaction pro forma remain unsupported. Post-period October draw remains distinct.

**CP-MODEL publication:** has populated annual source statements, separate supplement schedules, period/unit details, mapping suggestions, calculations, definitions and explicit gaps. It can publish the supported annual actuals once adapter rules preserve all distinctions above. It must retain the gap states and must not substitute missing periods or invented calculation definitions.

These are readiness assessments for bounded use, not a claim that any downstream consumer, runtime validation gate, full credit review or final deliverable has run. This is an intermediate analytical handoff.

spans.text: # CP-2E — TDG macro, hedging and absorbed ESG credit review
## Request
Assess interest-rate, FX, cost and ESG transmission to credit from the actual
FY2024 source and checked handoffs, including CP-2F's broader responsibilities.
Base balances are September 30, 2024; annual flows are October 1, 2023–September
30, 2024. USD millions unless noted. Derivative dates that were future at that
base remain historical scenarios; their subsequent outcomes have not been checked.
This is actual current-host-model analysis with local tools and conversation
context, not provider/API or imported owner execution.
**View: documented rate mitigation with dated protection changes; complete
macro-risk classification remains Insufficient Information.** The issuer reports
approximately 30 additional annual interest cost for a one-percentage-point rate
increase and approximately 77% fixed-rate gross debt. These are attributed
disclosures, not independently rebuilt net hedge results. Missing effective
exposure/FX/cost inputs prevent a calibrated overall sensitivity.
**ESG credit view:** remediation liabilities are a quantified historical
obligation with estimate uncertainty. Additional material deterioration is not
demonstrated. Environmental/physical/safety and transition channels warrant
specific monitoring; no ESG score, assumed greenium or invented debt ratchet is
assigned. Confidence is Medium for the bounded source interpretation.
## Sources
Actually opened CP-0, annual/quarterly CP-1, CP-1A, CP-1B, CP-1D, CP-2 and
CP-2D handoffs. Their exact paths/hashes are in
`CP-2E-attempt-1-calculations.json`. CP-1 supplies financial definitions and
facility data; CP-1A supplies business/governance context; CP-2/CP-1D supply
cash-conversion and recurring-cost reasoning; CP-2D supplies the actual quarterly
cash bridge and the access/forecast limits. None is replaced by memory or a fixture.
Original annual PDF SHA-256:
`dc6a8ea6249e4e919d190a4bbb459d9bf4eded005b7d5680ae911b32d44d44af`.
Short exact source excerpts and one-based PDF pages are retained in the
calculation record. Pages 151 (hedge terms) and 139 (remediation liabilities)
were rendered and visually checked; source images/hashes are retained.
Method selection: Deploy V-derived CP-2E and absorbed CP-2F analytical breadth
in the skill and its two method companions; later `src/deploy_vii/methods/cp2e.md`
and unchanged pure helpers provide applicable precision/missingness checks.
Hashes are retained in the calculation record. The descriptive T2F/T2G meanings
below follow the broader method, not the later runtime's different T2F mapping.
Historical quote limits and transport do not dictate source arithmetic or allow
facts to be relabelled to fit a synthetic example.
## Findings
### T2F.1 — source gate and evidence map
| Evidence | Source / date | Data and quality | Limitation / use |
| R | Annual PDF 54–55 / 2024-09-30 | Market-risk balances, reported rate/FX sensitivities; issuer disclosure | Reported sensitivities are not independently reconstructed scenarios. |
| H | PDF 150–152 / 2024-09-30 | Derivative programme, dated notional/strike schedules, hedge accounting and FX contracts | No full settlement/exposure attribution or independent legal review. |
| D | CP-1 debt register / 2024-09-30 | Principal, carrying amounts, terms and dates | Reporting amounts do not establish every debt/EBITDA functional currency. |
| O | PDF 17–19, 22–23 | Raw material, labour/production, physical, safety and transition risks | Risk disclosures identify mechanisms; they do not prove an event occurred or quantify elasticity. |
| E | PDF 139 / 2024-09-30 | Recorded environmental liabilities and estimate policy | Book liability is not future cash timing or an incremental stress loss. |
### T2F.2 — debt and rate exposure register
| Instrument | Principal / status | Rate basis / margin or coupon | Contractual maturity | Source / credit meaning |
| Tranche I | 1,871 | Floating, Term SOFR +2.75% alternative | 2028-08-24 | D; benchmark/floor/election and reset terms needed for exact shock. |
| Tranche J | 3,632 | Floating, Term SOFR +2.50% alternative | 2031-02-28 | D. |
| Tranche K | 1,699 | Floating, Term SOFR +2.75% alternative | 2030-03-22 | D. |
| Tranche L | 1,500 | Floating, Term SOFR +2.50% alternative | 2032-01-19 | D. |
| Securitization | Gross 487 / carrying 486 | Floating, three-month Term SOFR +1.45% | 2025-07-11 | R/H/D; collateral and extension terms matter. |
| 5.50% subordinated notes | 2,650 | Fixed 5.50% | 2027-11-15 | D; benchmark shock does not directly reprice contractual fixed coupon. |
| 4.625% subordinated notes | 1,200 | Fixed 4.625% | 2029-01-15 | D. |
| 4.875% subordinated notes | 750 | Fixed 4.875% | 2029-05-01 | D. |
| Revolver | Commitment 910; available 843; LC 67; funded draw not established | Floating draw terms; unused commitment is not a funded balance | 2029-02-27 | D; no funded amount of 67 is inferred. |

| Government advances / finance leases | 17 / 262 in debt note | Conditional repayment / lease obligations, not automatically SOFR exposure | Different terms; no single rate maturity imposed | D; do not classify all remaining debt as fixed or unhedged. |
Amounts are USD reporting equivalents. Contractual currency, functional earnings,
cash and covenant currencies are separate facts; complete mismatch analysis is
not inferred from a USD presentation column.
### T2F.3 — hedge schedule and coverage distinctions
| Instrument | Notional | Effective / maturity | Disclosed reference terms | Coverage / limitation |

| Swap | 500 | 2023-03-31 / 2025-03-31 | Reference fixed 3.00%; source illustrates 6.25% including then-stated 3.25% margin | H PDF 151; do not substitute the illustrated margin for current loan pricing. |
| Swap | 1,500 | 2023-03-31 / 2025-03-31 | Reference fixed 3.10%; source all-in illustration 6.35% | Same limitation. |
| Swap | 700 | 2023-03-31 / 2025-09-30 | Reference fixed 1.30%; source all-in illustration 4.55% | Same limitation. |
| Cap | 700 | 2023-03-31 / 2025-09-30 | Offsets three-month Term SOFR above 1.25% | Protection depends on exposure linkage/strike/reset; not a flat hedge ratio. |
| Collar | 1,100 | 2025-03-31 / 2026-09-30 | Floor 2.00%, ceiling 3.50% | Forward starting at September base; not current protection before start. |
| Collar | 500 | 2025-09-30 / 2026-09-30 | Floor 2.00%, ceiling 3.50% | Forward starting. |
| Collar | 1,338 | 2025-09-30 / 2027-09-30 | Floor 2.50%, ceiling 4.50% | Forward starting. |
| Collar | 1,550 | 2026-09-30 / 2027-09-30 | Floor 2.50%, ceiling 4.50% | Forward starting. |

| FX forwards | 120 USD-equivalent | Maximum duration twelve months from 2024-09-30 | Sell USD; Canadian dollar/euro contracts at trade-date spot equivalents | H PDF 152; currency transactions differ from all translated earnings. |
Active swap notionals sum to 2,700. Cap notional remains separately identified;
forward collars are not added to active coverage. No assumption that all
notionals cover distinct principal, or that accounting hedge effectiveness means
perfect economic protection. The company says derivative cash flows enter OCF,
and describes counterparty and credit-agreement-linked acceleration provisions
(PDF 150–151). Those are disclosed risks, not independent contract interpretation.
Derivative fair values are not protected debt principal.
### T2F.4 — baseline exposure and reconciliation limits
| Measure | Amount / status | Basis and creditor meaning |
| Identified floating principal | 9,189 | Calculated 8,702 term loans +487 securitization. Gross funded exposure before protection; no invented revolver draw. |
| Gross debt classification total | 25,068 | 24,581 debt-note gross items +487 separate securitization; distinct from carrying total 24,880. |
| Reported fixed-rate share | Approximately 77% | R PDF 55; attributed issuer classification, not 77% of floating debt. |

| Qualified hedged/unhedged floating exposure | Not Calculable from this review | Effective exposure attribution, floors/reference/reset dates, cap/collar overlap and relevant period need a complete reconstruction. |
| Unhedged percentage of total debt | Not Calculable | Neither a residual from 77% nor a ratio mixing principal and carrying amounts is substituted. |
### T2F.5 — rate sensitivity and conditional illustration
| Case | Result | Status / assumptions and limits |

| Issuer one-percentage-point rate increase | Approximately +30 annual interest cost | Reported R PDF 55 on outstanding September borrowings. Retained as issuer estimate, not independent after-hedge validation. |

| Gross principal ×1% arithmetic control | 91.89 = 9,189 ×0.01 | Arithmetic only. Not a qualified cash/net sensitivity: floor, reset, hedge and period details are unresolved. Difference from 30 is not forced into an invented hedge ratio. |
| Independent effective unhedged +100 bp impact | Not Calculable | Requires the effective unhedged base and schedule; a known source benchmark does not replace missing reconstruction inputs. |

| Conditional use of reported approximately-30 estimate | Approximately 1,188 cash interest; approximately 1,850 OCF-minus-capex proxy; approximately 3.51x As Defined / cash interest | Analyst illustration only: treat 30 as incremental annual cash interest, add once to FY2024 cash interest 1,158 and subtract once from proxy 1,880; hold all other flows/earnings fixed, no tax/WC feedback. Not a forecast, covenant ratio, true FCF or runway. |
The single-facility pure legacy calculation was actually called with the term-
loan balance 8,702, unknown floor/hedge ratio and missing FX EBITDA share. It
correctly returned missing rate/FX outcomes for those missing inputs. Its narrow
quote step cannot accept a balance of this magnitude under the documented 999.9999
limit; no unit rescaling, fake zero floor or source truncation was used to pass it.
The assumed 30 remains approximate; exact conditional arithmetic does not add
economic precision to the source estimate.
### T2F.6 — FX and natural-offset register
| Exposure | Source evidence / currency distinction | Mechanism and limitation |

| Revenue/operating translation | R PDF 55: foreign subsidiaries, primarily GBP/euro; consolidated reporting USD | Translation can change USD revenue/profit/assets without an identical cash impact. No currency EBITDA share is supplied. |

| Transaction exposure | H PDF 152: purchases/sales and USD-selling forwards for CAD/euro | Cash exposure depends on transaction currency, timing and offsets; the forward notional is not all foreign sales. |
| Geographic sales | O PDF 19: approximately 2.9 billion sales to foreign customers | Customer geography is not invoicing currency, foreign EBITDA share or a hedgeable net exposure base. |
| Natural hedges | Foreign revenues/costs and balances may offset; complete split not supplied | Partial offsets cannot be sized from geography. No numerical net exposure assumed. |

| Reported FX sensitivity | R PDF 55: a 10% FX change would not materially affect FY2024 net income | Attributed issuer conclusion; not zero, not EBITDA/debt sensitivity, and not proof of future protection. |

| Debt/cash/covenant and repatriation mismatch | Full denomination, functional-currency, location/access and covenant maps not supplied | Numeric debt/EBITDA/cash mismatch remains missing. No reporting-currency shortcut. |
### T2F.7 — raw materials, inflation and pass-through
| Driver | Evidence | Mechanism / creditor implication | Quantification and follow-up |

| Material/component cost or supply | O PDF 17–18: supplier disruptions, cost rises and certification constraints can impede replacement | Higher costs or interrupted output reduce margins/cash; inventory/qualification lags can absorb liquidity. | No spend volumes, cost elasticity or contractual indexation; no invented percentage shock. |

| Wages/labour/production | O PDF 17/19: skilled personnel, labour disagreements and supply-chain cost risks | Costs and delayed deliveries can weaken cash conversion, including customer OEM output effects. | Missing wage share, contractual recovery and timing. |

| Energy/freight/tariffs | O PDF 19: energy, transport and tariff-related supply/cost channels | Cost and availability shifts can raise cash demands and impair delivery; not all are commodity-price exposures. | No sourced cash-cost coefficients or hedge volumes. |

| Pass-through | O PDF 17 explicitly conditions impact on inability to pass increases to customers; CP-1A describes proprietary products | Proprietary content is a possible counterweight, not proof of price recovery without lag or demand effects. | Obtain contracts, realised price/cost bridge and timing before sizing net impact. |
### T2F.8 — macro synthesis and monitoring
| Driver | Transmission / contrary evidence | Dated condition or monitoring need |

| Rate/hedge changes | More unprotected repricing can consume cash; fixed coupons and disclosed derivatives mitigate selected exposure | At the historical base, 2025-03-31 and 2025-09-30 swap/cap expiries and collar starts change protection. Verify actual subsequent renewals/settlements rather than call them upcoming today. |

### Overall credit implication and CP-6 question
The macro downside is an adverse rate/reset or cost/demand move that reduces
cash conversion just as historical protection changes and obligations/distributions
compete for funds. Fixed coupons, derivatives, positive operating cash and
potential price recovery are real counterweights; their future adequacy is not
proved by notionals, source estimates or a qualitative business description.
The single best-supported CP-2F debate question is whether remediation estimate/
payment uncertainty could materially consume the post-distribution cash buffer.
The recorded liability supplies an actual baseline; it does not prove an
incremental loss, imminent funding call, default or recovery impairment. Current
cash-access and revised remediation evidence would strengthen or weaken that
concern. CP-6 should preserve the issuer's contrary cost expectation and avoid
an ESG-values judgement.
